items.explanation: 71-year-old man (b. 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 cardiology/cardiac-surgery visit and carried in every clinic note through 2026-07-28. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension; age 65-74; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). The only current medication documented in the chart is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; there is no current or past anticoagulant order for this patient and no documented contraindication or patient refusal. Prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure is coded but is not addressed anywhere as a reason to withhold anticoagulation. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC or warfarin.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at about 142/min with no discernible P waves (RR 348-720 ms), and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same, about 144/min (RR 344-648 ms). Both are atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The patient also has unspecified atrial fibrillation coded in the chart. The rate and rhythm documented in the note need correction and the rapid AF needs clinical attention (she was admitted the same evening and started on heparin/enoxaparin).

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler (clinic clinician) documents INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increases warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 2026-03-01 clinic memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician or clinic pharmacist, so it was due by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

Anticoagulation clinic note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD (clinic pharmacist, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) documents a home INR of 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. The 2026-03-01 clinic memo requires an INR within 7 days of such a dose change, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6); nothing is on file after the dose change, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24. She is 95 years old and also on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin, so the overdue recheck matters.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (it is absent from the 2025-08-02 medication list and appears from 2025-11-10 onward). Because the start pre-dates 3/1/2026, the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start - requirement met. (That ECG showed QTc about 513 ms; see the separate QT_SAFETY item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first order in the record; listed as a current medication from that visit onward). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (expressly preserved by the 2026-03-01 revision) and an ECG was due by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was recorded 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - requirement met. QTc on that tracing was about 420 ms.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (first order in the record; not on the 2025-12-15 medication list). The start is on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised 2026-03-01 memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded 2026-03-07, five days after the start, and the 2026-03-07 note documents its review - requirement met. QTc about 373 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (first escitalopram order in the record). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days - due by 2026-04-24. No ECG was obtained inside that window. The only ECG on file (107859369) was recorded 2026-04-29 during an unrelated encounter, 19 days after the start and 5 days after the deadline, so the requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue. (For information, that tracing showed QTc about 374 ms with limb-lead reversal suggested by the negative P/QRS in lead I.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (it is absent from the 2026-06-24 medication list; the only earlier exposure was a brief inpatient order in December 2025). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days - due by 2026-08-15. No ECG has been recorded since 2025-12-25, so the required post-start ECG is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (absent from the 2026-02-27 medication list). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - due by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart. However, the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 (DocumentReference/5e12a8aa-0439-53cd-a194-cc1a277d296d) records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18, which is inside the window; the report was requested by fax but has not been received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so the status cannot be determined until the report arrives - the report should be chased.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15 (absent from the 2026-06-05 medication list; earlier exposure was inpatient in early 2025). Start on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days - due by 2026-09-29, which is after the 2026-09-24 evaluation date, so the requirement is not yet due. No ECG has been obtained since 2025-03-09 (QTc about 406 ms); one should be scheduled before 2026-09-29.

80-year-old woman (b. 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 through 2026-05-28. CHA2DS2-VASc 9: CHF (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, acute on chronic combined systolic/diastolic heart failure), hypertension, age >=75 (2), diabetes mellitus type 2, prior stroke/TIA (2 - personal history of TIA/cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis, dysarthria and dysphagia following cerebral infarction), vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) and female sex. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, yet the only antithrombotic on the current medication list is aspirin 81 mg daily; there is no anticoagulant order at any time in the record and no documented contraindication. Aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

48-year-old man (b. 1978-02-27) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes from 2025-07-19 through 2026-06-12. CHA2DS2-VASc 2: congestive heart failure (congestive heart failure unspecified and acute systolic heart failure coded 2025-02-26, with other primary cardiomyopathy and prior cardiogenic shock/cardiac arrest) plus hypertension. Age 48 and male sex add nothing. A score of 2 in a man places him at >=2%/year thromboembolic risk, for which the 2023 AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. He had 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' coded during the June 2025 admissions, but there is no current outpatient anticoagulant order and the current medication list is famotidine and pantoprazole only. Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).

71-year-old woman (b. 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded during the March 2025 admission, at which she also had a cerebral infarction due to embolism of a cerebral artery with residual hemiparesis/ataxia. CHA2DS2-VASc 5: hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke (2) and female sex - anticoagulation is clearly recommended, and the stroke was cardioembolic. Her current medications through the 2026-07-10 clinic note are metoprolol, carvedilol and famotidine only; no anticoagulant has ever been ordered and no contraindication is documented. Her single ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with frequent ectopy, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily; the current order (authored 2026-08-20, supply through 2026-12-28) is active at the evaluation time. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this, the 2026-08-20 clinic note lists apixaban as continued (together with aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, i.e. triple therapy) and a new apixaban order was written the same day, with no documented cardiology decision that it was safe to resume. Anticoagulation plus dual antiplatelet therapy days after a transfusion-requiring ulcer bleed requires prescriber review.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order authored 2026-07-29, supply to 2027-01-05). His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT approximately 505 ms and Bazett QTc approximately 513 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo of 2025-01-15, so prescriber review is required. Electrolytes are not contributory: most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20). He is also on warfarin; amiodarone-warfarin interaction and QT should both be reviewed, and a repeat ECG is reasonable since the last tracing is 10 months old.

95-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation/flutter on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order authored 2026-08-22, supply to 2027-01-05). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows a regular rhythm at 58/min with QT approximately 530 ms and Bazett QTc approximately 520 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes (2026-02-14) potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL - magnesium is at the low end of normal and replacement could be considered. She also takes metoprolol succinate and amlodipine. A current ECG should be obtained because the tracing on file is over four years old.

35-year-old woman taking citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order authored 2026-05-29, supply to 2026-12-25). Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT approximately 475 ms and Bazett QTc approximately 515 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal. Note also that 40 mg daily exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended for citalopram in patients at risk of QT prolongation; dose reduction and a repeat ECG should be considered.

65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter has two overlapping oral anticoagulant orders active at the evaluation time: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (authored 2026-07-15, supply 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (authored 2026-07-15, supply 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 clinic note says the anticoagulant was being switched from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban order was not stopped and the note's own medication list contains both drugs. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban gives a markedly increased bleeding risk; the rivaroxaban order needs to be discontinued and the patient contacted to confirm which drug he is taking.

interpretations.explanation: 13df78e7 (66-year-old man, 2026-03-07). Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 81/min with an upright P wave (0.2 mV) in II/aVF preceding every QRS at a constant PR of 166 ms - normal sinus rhythm. QRS 75 ms with normal precordial progression, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 320 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms - well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold despite citalopram 40 mg daily. This is the patient's only ECG, so no prior comparison is possible. The finding agrees with the same-day clinic note ('ECG today: sinus rhythm').

568cb149 (47-year-old man at the time, 2025-07-15). Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 103/min with a clear upright P wave in II (0.22 mV) before every QRS, PR about 140 ms - sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia; no AF on this tracing despite his documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. QRS about 90 ms with deep S waves in V2-V3 and no bundle branch block; axis about +30 degrees (normal). QT about 350 ms, QTc about 465 ms (borderline prolonged). Prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147/min with a short QT and QTc in the 320-390 ms range, so the corrected QT has lengthened by more than 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60); note he received intravenous amiodarone around 2025-03-01.

5f3dcdb5 (45-year-old man, 2024-05-21). Regular rhythm at 110/min with a consistent low-amplitude upright P wave preceding each QRS (PR about 135 ms) - sinus tachycardia. QRS about 80 ms with an rS pattern in V1-V3 and no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +40 degrees (normal). QT roughly 330-350 ms giving a QTc of about 450 ms (upper normal/borderline). No prior ECG is on file for comparison.

5f74c4bf (78-year-old woman, 2026-06-10 19:36). Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 144/min (RR 344-648 ms, RMSSD 97 ms) with no discernible P waves and a fibrillatory baseline - atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about 0 to +5 degrees (normal). QT about 275 ms, QTc about 430 ms. The prior ECG 107914094, taken 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same day, shows the same rhythm (AF at about 142/min), so there is no change. Both tracings contradict the clinic note of the same day describing 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' - see the CONTRADICTION review item.

71a27b6b (83-year-old woman, 2025-08-02). Regular rhythm at 69/min with consistent atrial activity before each QRS (P best seen as a negative deflection in III, PR about 134 ms) - sinus rhythm. QRS 76 ms, no bundle branch block; tall R in I/aVL with deep S in III gives a frontal axis of about -25 degrees (still within the normal range). QT about 395 ms, QTc 423 ms. Prior ECG 104232242 (2025-04-27) showed the same rhythm at 60/min with QTc about 400 ms but with reversed limb-lead polarity (axis about -174 degrees); rhythm, conduction and QTc are unchanged.

735c5ea5 (56-year-old man, 2024-05-23). Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 97/min with an upright P wave in II before every QRS, PR about 118 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 62 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about 0 to +5 degrees (normal), with tall R waves in V4-V5. QT about 295 ms, QTc 377 ms. No prior ECG is available.

752d15e2 (56-year-old woman, 2025-12-25). Regular rhythm at 72/min with a consistent P wave before each QRS, PR about 130 ms - normal sinus rhythm. QRS 60 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +20 degrees (normal). QT about 340 ms, QTc 385 ms. No prior ECG for comparison. This remains her only tracing, which is why the ECG required after escitalopram was started on 2026-08-01 is recorded as overdue.

76202c51 (63-year-old woman at the time, 2024-11-15). Irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm, ventricular rate about 66/min (RR 694-1164 ms, RMSSD 308 ms), with a flat atrial baseline and no identifiable P waves (P-region amplitude 0.04 mV) - atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +25 degrees (normal). QT about 400 ms, QTc 425 ms. The prior ECG 107873952, three days earlier (2024-11-12), showed regular sinus rhythm at 69/min with a clear 0.22 mV P wave in II and QTc about 385 ms, so this tracing represents NEW_AF. She was loaded with amiodarone on 2024-11-13 and started on apixaban on 2024-12-10.

7ec7078a (50-year-old woman at the time, 2025-03-09). Regular rhythm at 58/min with a prominent upright P wave in II (0.2 mV) before each QRS, PR about 108 ms - sinus bradycardia. QRS 76 ms with a very deep S in V2 but no bundle branch block; axis about +58 degrees (normal). QT about 415 ms, QTc 410 ms. Prior ECG 106045460 (2025-03-08, one day earlier) was essentially identical (sinus 62/min, QTc about 430 ms); no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

807d2a03 (59-year-old woman, 2025-08-23). Regular rhythm at 83/min (RR 718-726 ms) with an upright P wave in II preceding every QRS, PR about 166 ms - normal sinus rhythm. QRS 55 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +51 degrees (normal). QT about 340 ms, QTc 402 ms. No prior ECG is on file.

8e77dd0b (47-year-old woman at the time, 2020-06-19). Regular sinus rhythm at 77/min with a well-formed upright P wave in II (0.27 mV), PR about 170 ms, QRS 58 ms, axis about +64 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 405 ms, QTc about 459 ms (borderline prolonged). The prior ECG 109048192 (2020-02-02) was sinus at 75/min with a markedly longer QT (QTc about 525-545 ms), so the corrected QT has shortened by more than 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60).

1cf9e585 (57-year-old man at the time, 2021-01-18). Regular rhythm at 121/min (RR 494-502 ms) with a low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave in II/aVF before each QRS, PR about 176 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 78 ms, no conduction block; axis about +41 degrees (normal). QT about 270 ms, QTc 385 ms. Compared with the prior ECG 106186980 (2016-09-16, sinus tachycardia 108/min, QRS 73 ms, QTc about 380 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

94abdf17 (48-year-old man, 2025-06-23). Regular rhythm at 54/min (RR 1074-1118 ms) with an upright P wave in II before every QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 210 ms - sinus bradycardia with first-degree AV block. QRS 72 ms with prominent Q waves in II/III/aVF and very tall R waves in V4-V5, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +39 degrees (normal). QT about 390 ms, QTc 372 ms. Prior ECG 103042067 (2024-11-30) was also sinus bradycardia (51/min) with a PR at the upper limit and QTc about 353 ms; rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc are unchanged.

a0bcbbc0 (58-year-old man at the time, 2025-09-13 07:17). Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 151/min (RR 312-604 ms, RMSSD 132 ms) with no organised P waves - atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; no measurable PR interval. QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about -5 degrees (normal). QT about 255 ms, QTc about 405 ms. The prior ECG 107374881 from the previous evening (2025-09-12 18:57) showed regular sinus rhythm at 77/min with a visible P wave and a single atrial ectopic beat, so this tracing represents NEW_AF - consistent with the intravenous amiodarone given on 2025-09-13 and the apixaban started 2025-10-30.

a6e7e991 (55-year-old woman, 2025-11-23). Regular sinus rhythm at 73/min with a clear upright P wave in II (0.22 mV) before each QRS, PR about 162 ms, QRS 76 ms, axis about +11 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 360 ms, QTc 398 ms. This confirms the clinic note of the same day ('ECG today: sinus rhythm'). The prior ECG 105362569 (2025-11-21) was also sinus at 67/min but with a markedly prolonged QT (QTc about 530 ms), so the corrected QT has shortened by well over 60 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60).

aeda7084 (64-year-old woman, 2025-02-15). Underlying regular sinus rhythm at about 73/min (RR 804-824 ms) with a consistent upright P wave and PR about 184 ms, interrupted by two pauses (RR 1314 ms and 1106 ms) at the end of the recording, suggesting sinus pauses or blocked atrial ectopics - the basic rhythm is sinus. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; large opposing deflections in I/III with a frontal axis about +34 degrees (normal). QT about 380 ms, QTc 418 ms. No prior ECG is available; the pauses merit clinical correlation.

b410dd44 (70-year-old man at the time, 2023-06-26). Regular rhythm at 112/min (RR 536-540 ms) with a well-formed upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) before every QRS, PR about 175 ms - sinus tachycardia; no atrial flutter on this tracing despite his coded atrial flutter. QRS 76 ms with a very deep S wave in V1-V2 and no bundle branch block; axis about +40 degrees (normal). QT about 280-310 ms, QTc about 388 ms. Prior ECG 102955795 (2022-07-04) was almost identical (sinus tachycardia 114/min, QTc about 385 ms); no changes.

b9a9ae7b (69-year-old woman, 2025-03-14). Dominant regular rhythm at about 62/min (sinus RR 936-998 ms) with an upright P wave preceding each conducted QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 215 ms - sinus rhythm with first-degree AV block. Two premature beats with compensatory pauses (RR 546/1362 ms and a 416/564 ms couplet) account for the overall RR irregularity; this is ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation (P waves remain organised, beat-to-beat P correlation 0.96). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -23 degrees (normal). QT about 380 ms, QTc 386 ms. This is her only ECG. Sinus rhythm here does not exclude her documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.

bbad4581 (41-year-old man, 2026-04-29). Regular rhythm at 69/min with consistent atrial activity before each QRS, PR about 150 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block. As recorded, lead I and lead II are dominantly negative while aVR is positive and the P waves are inverted in I/II, giving a computed frontal axis of about -175 degrees (extreme axis deviation); this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal and the tracing should be repeated with correct lead placement before the axis is accepted as real. QT about 350 ms, QTc 376 ms - reassuring given escitalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

bc2a74ce (32-year-old woman at the time, 2023-11-10). Regular sinus rhythm at 70/min with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR about 145 ms, QRS 88 ms, axis about +42 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The QT is prolonged at roughly 475-490 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 518 ms, above the 500 ms clinic threshold while she takes citalopram 40 mg daily - see the QT_SAFETY review item. The prior ECG 107149156 (2020-06-17) was sinus tachycardia at 133/min with a narrow QRS, right axis and a rate-corrected QT in a similar range, so no reliable change in rhythm, conduction or QTc can be established between the two.

c0d83ad6 (44-year-old man, 2026-03-08). Regular sinus rhythm at 68/min with an upright P wave in II, PR about 144 ms, QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +61 degrees (normal). QT about 395 ms, QTc 421 ms - below the watch-list threshold, which satisfies the ECG required after escitalopram was started on 2026-02-12. No prior ECG for comparison.

c4c29979 (67-year-old man at the time, 2019-01-13). Regular rhythm at 53/min (RR 1110-1170 ms) with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR about 174 ms - sinus bradycardia. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; tall R in I/aVL with a negative III gives a frontal axis of about -8 degrees (normal). QT about 385 ms, QTc 365 ms. Prior ECG 108651109 (2018-12-13) was sinus at 66/min with PR at the upper limit and QTc about 383 ms; no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

23069939 (53-year-old man at the time, 2023-10-08). Sinus rhythm at 68/min, upright P in II, PR 138 ms, QRS 80 ms, axis about +43 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. QT about 465 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 496 ms - prolonged but just below the 500 ms prescriber-review threshold in the clinic QT memo, which matters because he takes escitalopram. The prior ECG 100065910 (2022-11-23) was sinus at 75/min with QTc about 348 ms, so the QTc has risen by well over 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60); repeat tracing and review of QT-active drugs are advisable.

cb70e6ae (61-year-old man at the time, 2022-07-13). Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141/min (RR 404-454 ms, RMSSD 11 ms) with a small but consistent upright atrial deflection in II/aVF and V1 preceding each QRS at a fixed PR of about 140 ms, and a single atrial wave per cycle in the TP segment - sinus tachycardia rather than flutter or AF. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about 0 to +5 degrees (normal). QT about 260-270 ms, QTc about 408 ms. The prior ECG 109839112 (2022-07-11) showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at about 113/min with no P waves, so sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF).

dc332fb6 (69-year-old man, 2025-05-12). Regular sinus rhythm at 82/min with an upright P wave in II, PR about 148 ms, QRS about 95 ms with a normal R-wave progression and no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +25 degrees (normal). QT about 370 ms, QTc 435 ms. No prior ECG is available for comparison.

e1de99bc (81-year-old woman at the time, 2022-07-16). Regular sinus rhythm at 91/min with a consistent biphasic/negative P in V1 and upright P in II, PR about 140 ms, QRS 65 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +5 degrees (normal). QT about 330 ms, QTc 408 ms. Prior ECG 102616671 (2021-05-16) was sinus at 87/min with QTc about 388 ms; no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

e635f2dd (71-year-old man at the time, 2024-07-17). Regular rhythm at 61/min with an upright P wave in II before each QRS, PR about 190 ms - sinus rhythm. The QRS is wide at about 120-125 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V6, absent septal q waves and a small r with a deep broad S in V1-V3: left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -26 degrees (within the normal range). QT about 425 ms, QTc 435 ms. The prior ECG 103686933 (2024-06-03) shows the identical wide-QRS left bundle branch block pattern at 68/min with QTc about 445 ms, so there is no new conduction abnormality and no significant QTc change.

f3fc719c (21-year-old woman, 2025-03-19). Regular rhythm at 102/min with an upright P wave in II before every QRS, PR about 162 ms - sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia. QRS 70 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +40 degrees (normal). QT about 320 ms, QTc 419 ms. Prior ECG 101016166 (2025-03-18, the previous day) was essentially the same (sinus 102/min, QTc about 420 ms); no changes.

f572075b (81-year-old man, 2025-09-22). Regular sinus rhythm at 66/min with an upright P wave in II, PR about 176 ms, QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block. Lead I and aVL are dominantly positive with a negative III and aVF, giving a frontal axis of about -27 degrees - at the border of but still within the normal range (borderline left axis). Precordial voltages are strikingly low in V4-V6. QT about 365 ms, QTc 382 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

f77a5b72 (91-year-old woman at the time, 2022-04-27). Regular rhythm at 58/min (RR 970-1100 ms) with a low-amplitude but consistent upright P wave in II/aVF before each QRS at a PR of about 196 ms - sinus bradycardia (she is on amiodarone and metoprolol). QRS 72 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +20 to +35 degrees (normal). The QT is markedly prolonged at about 530 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 525 ms, above the 500 ms clinic threshold on amiodarone - see the QT_SAFETY review item. The prior ECG 100867733 (2022-04-06) showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation at about 129/min with no P waves and a much shorter corrected QT, so sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has lengthened by more than 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60).

fa5fbf9c (84-year-old woman at the time, 2022-05-01). Regular rhythm at 107/min (RR 552-564 ms) with an upright P wave in II (0.21 mV) before each QRS, PR about 160 ms - sinus tachycardia. QRS 55 ms, no bundle branch block; axis about +49 degrees (normal). QT about 330 ms, QTc about 445 ms. Prior ECG 107274479 (2019-07-27) was sinus at 75/min with QTc about 410-425 ms; rhythm and conduction are unchanged and the QTc difference is under 60 ms.

28dcf33b (53-year-old woman, 2024-04-19). Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 121/min with a consistent upright P wave in II/aVF before each QRS (PR 176 ms) - sinus tachycardia. 74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily; the current order (authored 2026-08-20, supply through 2026-12-28) is active at the evaluation time. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Anticoagulation plus dual antiplatelet therapy days after a transfusion-requiring ulcer bleed requires prescriber review.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at about 142/min with no discernible P waves (RR 348-720 ms), and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same, about 144/min (RR 344-648 ms). Both are atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The patient also has unspecified atrial fibrillation coded in the chart. The rate and rhythm documented in the note need correction and the rapid AF needs clinical attention (she was admitted the same evening and started on heparin/enoxaparin).

80-year-old woman (b. 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 through 2026-05-28. CHA2DS2-VASc 9: CHF (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, acute on chronic combined systolic/diastolic heart failure), hypertension, age >=75 (2), diabetes mellitus type 2, prior stroke/TIA (2 - personal history of TIA/cerebral infarction with residual hemiparesis, dysarthria and dysphagia following cerebral infarction), vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) and female sex. CHA2DS2-VASc 2: congestive heart failure (congestive heart failure unspecified and acute systolic heart failure coded 2025-02-26, with other primary cardiomyopathy and prior cardiogenic shock/cardiac arrest) plus hypertension. Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).

71-year-old woman (b. 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded during the March 2025 admission, at which she also had a cerebral infarction due to embolism of a cerebral artery with residual hemiparesis/ataxia. CHA2DS2-VASc 5: hypertension, age 65-74, prior stroke (2) and female sex - anticoagulation is clearly recommended, and the stroke was cardioembolic. Her current medications through the 2026-07-10 clinic note are metoprolol, carvedilol and famotidine only; no anticoagulant has ever been ordered and no contraindication is documented. Her single ECG (2025-03-14) shows sinus rhythm with frequent ectopy, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily; the current order (authored 2026-08-20, supply through 2026-12-28) is active at the evaluation time. Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with a haemoglobin nadir of 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite this, the 2026-08-20 clinic note lists apixaban as continued (together with aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg, i.e. triple therapy) and a new apixaban order was written the same day, with no documented cardiology decision that it was safe to resume. Anticoagulation plus dual antiplatelet therapy days after a transfusion-requiring ulcer bleed requires prescriber review.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current order authored 2026-07-29, supply to 2027-01-05). Electrolytes are not contributory: most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20). The only current medication documented in the chart is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; there is no current or past anticoagulant order for this patient and no documented contraindication or patient refusal. Prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure is coded but is not addressed anywhere as a reason to withhold anticoagulation. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC or warfarin.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both are atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The patient also has unspecified atrial fibrillation coded in the chart. The rate and rhythm documented in the note need correction and the rapid AF needs clinical attention (she was admitted the same evening and started on heparin/enoxaparin).

INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).

Anticoagulation plus dual antiplatelet therapy days after a transfusion-requiring ulcer bleed requires prescriber review.

interpretations.explanation: 13df78e7 (66-year-old man, 2026-03-07). QRS 75 ms with normal precordial progression, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 320 ms, Bazett QTc 378 ms - well below the 500 ms watch-list threshold despite citalopram 40 mg daily. This is the patient's only ECG, so no prior comparison is possible. The finding agrees with the same-day clinic note ('ECG today: sinus rhythm').

568cb149 (47-year-old man at the time, 2025-07-15). QRS about 90 ms with deep S waves in V2-V3 and no bundle branch block; axis about +30 degrees (normal). QT about 350 ms, QTc about 465 ms (borderline prolonged). Prior ECG 100698634 (2025-06-20) was sinus tachycardia at 147/min with a short QT and QTc in the 320-390 ms range, so the corrected QT has lengthened by more than 60 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60); note he received intravenous amiodarone around 2025-03-01.

No prior ECG is on file for comparison.

5f74c4bf (78-year-old woman, 2026-06-10 19:36). 735c5ea5 (56-year-old man, 2024-05-23). Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 97/min with an upright P wave in II before every QRS, PR about 118 ms - sinus rhythm. QRS 68 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -45 degrees (left axis deviation, consistent with left anterior fascicular block). QT about 315 ms, QTc 412 ms. This is his only ECG, so no prior comparison.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man (b. 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 cardiology/cardiac-surgery visit and carried in every clinic note through 2026-07-28. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension; age 65-74; vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). The only current medication documented in the chart is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; there is no current or past anticoagulant order for this patient and no documented contraindication or patient refusal. Prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure is coded but is not addressed anywhere as a reason to withhold anticoagulation. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC or warfarin.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at about 142/min with no discernible P waves (RR 348-720 ms), and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same, about 144/min (RR 344-648 ms). Both are atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The patient also has unspecified atrial fibrillation coded in the chart. The rate and rhythm documented in the note need correction and the rapid AF needs clinical attention (she was admitted the same evening and started on heparin/enoxaparin).

Cardiology clinic note of 2026-09-01 by Dr. Paul Kessler (clinic clinician) documents INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increases warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 2026-03-01 clinic memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician or clinic pharmacist, so it was due by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

Anticoagulation clinic note of 2026-09-10 by L. Nguyen, PharmD (clinic pharmacist, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) documents a home INR of 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. The 2026-03-01 clinic memo requires an INR within 7 days of such a dose change, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6); nothing is on file after the dose change, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24. She is 95 years old and also on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin, so the overdue recheck matters.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10 (it is absent from the 2025-08-02 medication list and appears from 2025-11-10 onward). 80-year-old woman (b. 1945-10-26) with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 2025-09-12 through 2026-05-28. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, yet the only antithrombotic on the current medication list is aspirin 81 mg daily; there is no anticoagulant order at any time in the record and no documented contraindication. Aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).

The only current medication documented in the chart is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; there is no current or past anticoagulant order for this patient and no documented contraindication or patient refusal. Prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure is coded but is not addressed anywhere as a reason to withhold anticoagulation. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC or warfarin.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (2026-06-10 17:13) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at about 142/min with no discernible P waves (RR 348-720 ms), and 103088543 (2026-06-10 19:36) shows the same, about 144/min (RR 344-648 ms). Both are atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The patient also has unspecified atrial fibrillation coded in the chart. The rate and rhythm documented in the note need correction and the rapid AF needs clinical attention (she was admitted the same evening and started on heparin/enoxaparin).

Under the 2026-03-01 clinic memo an INR is required within 7 days of a warfarin dose change made by a Cardiology Clinic clinician or clinic pharmacist, so it was due by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

Nguyen, PharmD (clinic pharmacist, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) documents a home INR of 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. No INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6); nothing is on file after the dose change, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24. She is 95 years old and also on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin, so the overdue recheck matters.

Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. The rate and rhythm documented in the note need correction and the rapid AF needs clinical attention (she was admitted the same evening and started on heparin/enoxaparin).

Aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

He had 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' coded during the June 2025 admissions, but there is no current outpatient anticoagulant order and the current medication list is famotidine and pantoprazole only. Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).

Anticoagulation plus dual antiplatelet therapy days after a transfusion-requiring ulcer bleed requires prescriber review.

arguments.explanation: bbad4581 (41-year-old man, 2026-04-29). Regular rhythm at 69/min with consistent atrial activity before each QRS, PR about 150 ms - sinus rhythm. The only current medication documented in the chart is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; there is no current or past anticoagulant order for this patient and no documented contraindication or patient refusal. Prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure is coded but is not addressed anywhere as a reason to withhold anticoagulation. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC or warfarin.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both are atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. The patient also has unspecified atrial fibrillation coded in the chart. The rate and rhythm documented in the note need correction and the rapid AF needs clinical attention (she was admitted the same evening and started on heparin/enoxaparin).

INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

No INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6); nothing is on file after the dose change, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24. She is 95 years old and also on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin, so the overdue recheck matters.

Anticoagulation is strongly recommended, yet the only antithrombotic on the current medication list is aspirin 81 mg daily; there is no anticoagulant order at any time in the record and no documented contraindication. Aspirin monotherapy is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

CHA2DS2-VASc 2: congestive heart failure (congestive heart failure unspecified and acute systolic heart failure coded 2025-02-26, with other primary cardiomyopathy and prior cardiogenic shock/cardiac arrest) plus hypertension. Age 48 and male sex add nothing. A score of 2 in a man places him at >=2%/year thromboembolic risk, for which the 2023 AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. He had 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' coded during the June 2025 admissions, but there is no current outpatient anticoagulant order and the current medication list is famotidine and pantoprazole only. Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).

Her current medications through the 2026-07-10 clinic note are metoprolol, carvedilol and famotidine only; no anticoagulant has ever been ordered and no contraindication is documented. Note also that 40 mg daily exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended for citalopram in patients at risk of QT prolongation; dose reduction and a repeat ECG should be considered.

The only current medication documented in the chart is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; there is no current or past anticoagulant order for this patient and no documented contraindication or patient refusal. Prior hemorrhage complicating a procedure is coded but is not addressed anywhere as a reason to withhold anticoagulation. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC or warfarin.

The rate and rhythm documented in the note need correction and the rapid AF needs clinical attention (she was admitted the same evening and started on heparin/enoxaparin).

Age 48 and male sex add nothing. A score of 2 in a man places him at >=2%/year thromboembolic risk, for which the 2023 AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation. He had 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' coded during the June 2025 admissions, but there is no current outpatient anticoagulant order and the current medication list is famotidine and pantoprazole only. Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).

He had 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' coded during the June 2025 admissions, but there is no current outpatient anticoagulant order and the current medication list is famotidine and pantoprazole only. Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).

The rate and rhythm documented in the note need correction and the rapid AF needs clinical attention (she was admitted the same evening and started on heparin/enoxaparin).

INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, four days after the change - requirement met.

Nguyen, PharmD (clinic pharmacist, acting under the anticoagulation standing order) documents a home INR of 3.4 and decreases warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. The 2026-03-01 clinic memo requires an INR within 7 days of such a dose change, i.e. by 2026-09-17. No INR has been resulted since 2026-08-22 (2.6); nothing is on file after the dose change, so the follow-up INR is overdue as of 2026-09-24. She is 95 years old and also on amiodarone, which potentiates warfarin, so the overdue recheck matters.

He had 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' coded during the June 2025 admissions, but there is no current outpatient anticoagulant order and the current medication list is famotidine and pantoprazole only. Needs review to restart/initiate anticoagulation (note concurrent acid suppression and no documented bleeding).
